page.layout: One printed page with a single column of running text, with no margin notes, catchword or signature. Running head at top, page number at top left.

main_text.p: tioni omnibus fuit,ita gloria atque opi-bus in dies magis ac magis crevit, cum interim Græciæ decus Athenæ ,& reli-quæ hujus gentis civitates præfidiis aut imperio Macedonum gravatæ cum adhuc ingemiscerent. In eo secundæ fortunæ curfu, adspirante regum amicorum gratiâ, refectis jam iis quæ bello diruta aut vitiata fuerant, operâ & ingenio Charetis Lindii ingentem illum Coloflùm,de quo diximus ante,inchoavit,& duodecennio perfecit, opus admirandum,quo & artifex,& civitas & tota infula celebritatem meruére. Initium operis hujus factum annis quasi xiii post bellum Demetrianum folutum, cum numerarent Romaniannum urbis ccccLxiii[?],qui concurrebat cum Olympiadis cxxii anno secundo & tertio. Is Coloflus Soli dicatus, cui infula sacrata erat,cum abfoluto opere stetisset annos, ut Plinius ait, lvi, ingenti terræ motu quassatus, fractis genibus concidit: fi. multque multa præclara urbis ædificia & ornamenta publica privataq; eodem terræ tremore concussa corruerunt. Un-de ingens dolor ac detrimentum civitati extitit. Sed affirmat Polybius, tam sapienter hac calamitate usam esse civitatem, ut in dolore commotis animis regum, & amicorum, eorundem beneficentia

page.notes: Printed page 184, running head "DESCRIPTIO". Single column, no marginal notes. The first word is a fragment ("tioni", from "gloria" ... "opi-"), so the paragraph continues from the previous page. Doubtful readings: "ccccLxiii" (the numeral in the scan is hard to read, marked [?]). "Romaniannum" is copied as printed. The scan shows faint partial letters at the left edge ("ne", "mor", "ni") and shadow lines at the right edge. These are show-through or the edge of the neighbouring page and are not transcribed. Printed spellings such as "fuit,ita", "Coloflùm", "Coloflus" and "fi." are kept as printed.
